name: Custom Packaging Labels
seoTitle: Custom Packaging Labels for Boxes, Jars and Bottles
seoDescription: Custom packaging labels on BOPP, vinyl, paper or kraft, matched to jars, bottles, boxes and mailers. Rolls or sheets, barcodes and batch codes, free proof.
tagline: Product, box and jar labels on the right stock for the package, in rolls or sheets.
quickAnswer: Custom packaging labels are printed, adhesive labels made for product packaging: boxes, jars, bottles, pouches, tins and mailers. We print them on white or clear BOPP, vinyl, gloss or matte paper and kraft, in rolls for applicators or sheets for hand application, with barcodes and batch codes if needed. From $0.30 per label, 100 minimum, 5 to 7 business days production.
highlights: Finish: gloss, matte, spot UV, laminate

sections.h2: One label stock does not suit a jar, a box and a mailer
sections.html:
A candle jar sits in a warm room and gets handled with oily fingers. A shipping box is dry cardboard that goes out the door once. A cold-brew bottle sweats in a fridge. Each of those needs a different label stock, and sorting that out is what this page is for. The sibling product, our die cut labels range, is about shape: a label cut to the outline of a logo or illustration. Packaging labels are about the package. We start from the surface, the storage conditions and how the label will be applied, then choose stock, adhesive and format to match. The shape can still be anything, but it is the last decision rather than the first.

Typical orders are front and back labels for food and cosmetic jars, box seals and brand labels for shipping cartons, lid labels for tins, ingredient panels for pouches and hang-tag style labels for bags.

sections.h2: Match the stock to the package it lives on
sections.html:
Use this table as a starting point. Surface and conditions decide the material; the finish is mostly a look.

Shipping cartons and mailersGloss or matte paperDry, short-lived surface; paper is the economical choiceUncoated matte or gloss

Clear BOPP on glass gives the "no label" look where only the print shows; add a white ink layer under light colors so they do not vanish against dark contents.

sections.h2: What usually has to go on the label, and the space it takes
sections.html:
Front labels carry the brand; back and side labels carry the information. Plan the size around the mandatory text before you shrink it to fit a pretty shape.

  • Barcode (UPC/EAN): at least 1.0" wide by 0.5" tall at full height, printed in black on white or a pale background, never on kraft or clear without a white block behind it.
  • Ingredient and allergen panel: 6 pt minimum type, which on a 2" x 3" back label gives room for roughly 60 words.
  • Net weight or volume: on the front, lower third, in a size that reads at arm's length.
  • Batch, lot or best-by code: leave a blank 0.75" x 0.3" box for an inkjet or hand stamp, or send us a data file and we print the variable text.
  • QR code: 0.8" square minimum, with quiet space around it, tested on the proof before the run.
  • Warnings and recycling marks: small but legally required on many categories; cosmetics, candles and supplements each have their own rules.

Our free design support will lay out the panel so the type stays legal and readable, and the Die Cut Stickers home page lists the other formats if a label will not hold everything.

sections.h2: Cold rooms, oily hands and leaking lids: where paper gives up
sections.html: Paper labels are fine on a dry box. They are the wrong choice on anything that gets wet, chilled or greasy. A paper label on a fridge-stored jar bubbles within a week; a paper label on a soap bar wrapper goes soft in a steamy bathroom; a paper label on a candle wrinkles when the wax warms. For those, use BOPP or vinyl with a laminate, which wipes clean and does not absorb oil. Freezer labels need a cold-temp adhesive applied before the pack goes in, since standard adhesives will not bond below about 40°F. If the package will sit outside, on a planter, a propane tank or a cooler, the films on the outdoor sticker page are the better fit, since they are rated for sun as well as water.

sections.h2: Rolls or sheets: decide by how you will apply them
sections.html: Rolls suit anyone using a hand or tabletop applicator, or labeling more than a few hundred units a week: the liner feeds, the label peels at the plate, and placement stays consistent. We wind rolls on a 3" core by default and can set the unwind direction for your machine. Sheets suit hand application in a small kitchen or studio; peel one at a time, and there is no spare roll stock to store. Singles, each label on its own backing, make sense for large box labels or labels that get packed with a kit for the customer to apply. Say which you need at quoting, because roll labels are die cut with the liner intact and sheet labels are kiss cut, and the two are set up differently on press.

sections.h2: Ordering packaging labels for a product line
sections.html:
1. List every package in the line with its surface, dimensions and the conditions it will see: fridge, bathroom, warehouse, retail shelf.
  2. Measure the flat label area. On a round jar, measure the circumference and leave at least 0.25" of gap so the ends never overlap.
  3. Pick the stock from the table above and the adhesive: permanent for retail and food, removable for reusable containers or sample jars.
  4. Send artwork as PDF, AI, EPS or SVG with 0.125" bleed, or 300 dpi PNG or JPG at final size. Pantone references are welcome for brand colors.
  5. Choose rolls, sheets or singles, and tell us the quantity per design. The minimum is 100 labels per design, and several SKUs can share one order.
  6. Check the free digital proof for barcode size, legal text and cut line, then approve. Production runs 5 to 7 business days, with free FedEx shipping in the United States.

Prices start at $0.30 per label and drop with quantity; a quote for the whole line is quicker than quoting SKU by SKU, so send the quote form for packaging labels everything at once.

faqs.q: Which packaging label material works on a glass jar that goes in the fridge?
faqs.a: White or clear BOPP with a laminate. It does not absorb condensation, so the label stays flat when the jar sweats, and it wipes clean of oils and sauces. Paper labels on a refrigerated jar bubble and peel within days, so avoid them for anything chilled.

faqs.q: Can packaging labels be printed with barcodes and batch codes?
faqs.a: Yes. Static barcodes are printed as part of the artwork. For batch numbers, best-by dates or sequential codes, send a spreadsheet and we print the variable text on each label. If you stamp codes in-house, we leave a blank box on the label sized for your printer or stamp.

faqs.q: Do you supply packaging labels on rolls for a label applicator?
faqs.a: Yes. Rolls are wound on a 3" core by default, with the unwind direction set to match your applicator, and the label gap and liner width are set to the machine's spec. Tell us the applicator model or send its roll requirements and we match them on the proof.

faqs.q: How do I size a wrap-around label for a round bottle or candle jar?
faqs.a: Measure the circumference with a tape, then subtract at least 0.25" so the ends do not overlap, and measure the straight-sided height between the shoulder and the base curve. Labels placed over a taper will wrinkle, so keep the label on the straight section of the container.

faqs.q: Will a packaging label survive hot candle wax or a warm bathroom?
faqs.a: On vinyl or BOPP with a laminate, yes. The film does not soften from the warmth of a burning candle jar, and it shrugs off the steam and splashes around a sink. Use permanent adhesive on glass and tins, and ask for matte laminate if the label will be handled with wet hands.

faqs.q: Are clear packaging labels really invisible on glass?
faqs.a: Close to it. Clear BOPP shows the print with no visible edge once applied, giving the printed-on-the-jar look. Light colors and white text need a white ink layer underneath or they disappear against dark contents, and we show that layer on the proof so you can check it.

faqs.q: Can I order packaging labels in kraft paper to match a kraft box?
faqs.a: Yes. Kraft paper labels print well in dark inks and black, and the brown shows through lighter colors, which is part of the look. They are for dry packaging such as bakery boxes, gift boxes and coffee bags with an inner liner; for anything damp, choose a film with a kraft-look print instead.

faqs.q: What is the smallest quantity of packaging labels per product?
faqs.a: 100 labels per design. A line with five SKUs can go on one order at 100 of each, sharing the setup, and the price per label falls as the total rises. Prices start at $0.30 per label, set by size, stock and quantity, and we quote the whole line together.

faqs.q: Can a packaging label be applied to a freezer pack?
faqs.a: Yes, with a cold-temperature adhesive and the label applied while the pack is still at room temperature. Standard adhesives stop bonding below about 40°F, so a label stuck onto an already frozen pack will lift. Film stock is the right choice; paper goes soft when the pack thaws.

faqs.q: Do packaging labels come in sheets for hand application?
faqs.a: Yes. Kiss cut sheets let you peel one label at a time, which suits small kitchens, studios and anyone applying a few dozen a day. There is no liner waste to manage and no roll to store. Switch to rolls once you are labeling a few hundred units a week.

faqs.q: Are the inks on packaging labels safe for food packaging?
faqs.a: Our labels are applied to the outside of the package and the inks are not in contact with the food. For direct food contact you would need a specific food-grade construction, so tell us if the label will touch the product itself and we will advise on the right stock.

faqs.q: How quickly can I get packaging labels for a product launch?
faqs.a: Standard production is 5 to 7 business days after you approve the proof, with free FedEx shipping in the United States and delivery inside 8 to 10 business days. Rush production is available on request, so say your launch date when you ask for a quote and we will tell you what is possible.
